title: Stream & Tool-call Interop Canary + Contract Orchestra
creator: Asha Menon
description: Run a lightweight, automated canary and contract orchestration that validates end-to-end behavior for streaming responses, tool/function calls, and structured outputs across supported API compatibility layers. Focus on producing stable failure fingerprints and actionable CI signals rather than exhaustive coverage. Deliver a reusable harness, a curated prompt/workflow corpus, and CI gates that block regressions in protocol semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Canary suite runs in CI within 9 minutes and fails with clear error codes when breaking changes occur
Harness verifies: streaming chunk ordering, stream chunk semantics (delta vs final), tool-call initiation/termination events, tool-annotation metadata, and structured output schema stability
Automated mapping from failing canaries to suggested rollback (model variant) or fallback policies stored in the incident dashboard
Test corpus covers at least 12 representative multi-tool workflows (chat->tool->structured-output) and is review-approved by API and SDK owners
New CI gate added to main branch: block merge if 3 or more canary tests fail for two consecutive runs
test_plan: 1) Implement small harness service that drives an API client across compatibility layers (legacy REST, streaming websocket, new multiplexed stream)
2) Build 12 multi-tool workflows: search->func-call->rerank, file-ops->toolchain, structured-invoice->json-schema, etc.
3) Add schema-validating assertions for structured outputs (JSON-schema and strict field presence)
4) Simulate partial network interruptions and assert graceful tool-call resume/fallback
5) Integrate the harness with CI (self-hosted runner) and add slide-level dashboards for failures
implementation_notes: Prefer deterministic seeds for prompt variability to reduce non-deterministic test flakes
Use lightweight mocked tool endpoints for most workflows, with 2 end-to-end tests hitting staging tool infra
Expose configurable timeouts and backoff policies in the harness for environment tuning
Record full protocol traces (timestamps, event types) for each run and store artifacts in GCS for triage
Leverage existing streaming client libs in sdk-js and sdk-py; contribute small adapter for multiplexed streams
risks: Flaky tests due to nondeterministic model outputs; mitigated via focused assertions on protocol metadata and structural fields
CI runtime budget blowout — keep the canary fast (<9m) and run full corpus nightly instead of per-PR
Potential false positives on schema changes; introduce explicit schema versioning and a migration acceptance path
